The Boost Quiz is, as its name implies, a quiz segment consisting of five questions that appears in each story of Xeno-comi. Most questions are related to the chapter's events, serving to test whether the player has been paying attention to the story. However, some questions may also draw from entries in the . The player has 10 seconds to answer each question. If the time runs out or the player selects an incorrect answer, the same question will be repeated until the correct answer is chosen. If all five answers are answered correctly on the first try, a special CG image will be unlocked.

Casual Mode is a gameplay option in Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition and Future Connected. It drastically decreases the difficulty of battles without reducing rewards or gating progress, allowing players to enjoy the story and complete any combat task with minimal effort and no penalties. If the player suffers defeat twice in quick succession, the game will suggest enabling Casual Mode, unless tutorial pop-ups are disabled. Catalyst is the community-created term to refer to a Legendary Blade in Xenoblade Chronicles 2, whose weapon has the unique class of Catalyst Scimitar, revealed and obtained during . The term arose due to a desire to mask a major spoiler, and continues to be used despite some official material treating the matter as an open secret. As per this wiki's spoiler policy, while some effort will be made to use this term if feasible, perfect secrecy cannot be guaranteed. It is inevitable that something will spoil the issue in the interest of correct and complete information. To continue to the page on the subject, click here.

COSMOS is a track from the music of Xenosaga Episode I. It plays in the main menu of the Xenosaga Premium Disc. The track is a looped version of the stock music of the same name, released on the 1st of October, 1997 as part of the [https://www.nash.jp/nml/ Nash Music Library]. This makes it one of very few tracks in the series not to have been composed for the game it appears in; while the series' music often samples stock music and sounds, stock music is very rarely used unedited as an entire track.

Class Points, shortened to CP, are a mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. When a character earns enough CP, their current increases in rank. A character's CP is represented in the UI by a thin lilac bar below their blue bar. When they gain CP, the amount gained appears above their head in the overworld. If a character's current Class cannot be ranked up (e.g. due to having reached the rank cap of 10 or 20), they earn no CP. Heroes and Future Redeemed characters also earn no CP. Different Classes have different CP thresholds per rank. They are listed in the "Levelling" table in the Data section of each relevant Class's page. Combat or battle is a central gameplay mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and Torna ~ The Golden Country. The game uses a real-time battle system which takes place in the overworld. Combat initiates when a party member attacks an enemy or vice versa. This results in several immediate changes to gameplay: * The display changes to the combat display (which hides the map and compass and shows the enemy HP and characters' attacks, among other things). * Entering the in-game menu is disabled; the buttons used to enter the menu perform other functions. Contracts are key items in Xenoblade Chronicles 2. They are received by completing certain event, non-repeatable, Merc Missions. Each contract will unlock a specific pouch item to be sold at a lifestyle and represents the trading relations between two of Alrest's nations. As an example, the Adventures Contract is obtained by completing Long-Awaited Work and allows Reedirait Bookstore to sell Adventures of Myram. Contracts are inherently linked to deeds, as obtaining as many contracts as possible will make more deeds available for purchase as new items are put up for sale at shops.
